findings.title: load('sotus') returns the nips_model sklearn Pipeline instead of the documented SOTU speeches; hyp.plot(hyp.load('sotus')) crashes
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
sotus = hyp.load('sotus')
print(type(sotus))  # <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>
hyp.plot(sotus)     # TypeError
# registry check:
# grep -n "'sotus'\|'nips_model'" hypertools/io/load.py
# md5 ~/hypertools_data/sotus ~/hypertools_data/nips_model

findings.title: Static line plots silently resample every trajectory to ~frame_rate*duration (~900) vertices: a 50-sigma single-sample spike in 10,000-sample data is completely absent from the default plot, and the final ~0.1% of samples are never drawn (both backends)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
d = np.cumsum(rng.standard_normal((10000,3)), axis=0)*0.05
d[5001] += np.array([50.,50.,50.])
fig = hyp.plot(d, reduce=None, show=False)
X,Y,Z = fig.axes[0].lines[0].get_data_3d()
print(X.shape)  # (900,) not (10000,)
# compare fig.savefig(...) against plain ax.plot(d[:,0],d[:,1],d[:,2])
findings.expected: A static line plot of N samples draws all N samples (or documents/warns about lossy resampling); genuine extreme samples are visible; the trajectory endpoint is drawn.
findings.actual:
vertices: 900
true max coord: 53.88  drawn max coord: 1.0
[spike_hypertools.png: no spike visible; spike_groundtruth.png: needle to (50,50,50) dominates]
plotly trace0: scatter3d n points: 900
10000-sample, +500 on LAST sample: 99th pct of |drawn| coords = 0.920 (endpoint excluded); last interp grid point = index 9987.9 of 9999

findings.title: duration= and frame_rate= are documented '(animation only)' but silently reshape STATIC plots -- duration=1, frame_rate=2 draws a 10,000-sample trajectory as a single 2-vertex segment
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(5).standard_normal((10000,3)), axis=0)
for dur, fr in [(30,30),(60,30),(1,2)]:
    fig = hyp.plot(d, reduce=None, duration=dur, frame_rate=fr, show=False)
    print(dur, fr, fig.axes[0].lines[0].get_data_3d()[0].shape)
findings.expected: Parameters documented '(animation only)' have no effect on a non-animated plot.
findings.actual:
static plot duration=30 frame_rate=30 -> 900 vertices
static plot duration=60 frame_rate=30 -> 1800 vertices
static plot duration=1 frame_rate=2 -> 2 vertices

findings.title: align() silently accepts 3D arrays, flattening them into (n_slices, time*channels); on realistic sizes this grinds for ~1 minute and returns meaningless output instead of raising a shape error
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
bad = [np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((2,100,3)) for _ in range(2)]
out = hyp.align(bad)
print(np.asarray(out[0]).shape)  # (2, 300) -- no error, no warning
# slow variant: bad = [np.random.standard_normal((2,1000,3))]*2 -> ~59 s
findings.expected: ValueError naming the offending dataset's ndim/shape and stating that align expects 2D (samples x features) datasets.
findings.actual:
align 3D arrays: ACCEPTED, 0.073s, out[0] shape (2, 300)
[workflow log] W3b align [spiral(2,1000,3) misshaped, rotated]: 58.703s

findings.title: reduce() unknown-model error message embeds raw multi-line-string whitespace, points to a stale http:// readthedocs URL, and (unlike align's) does not list the supported model names
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.reduce(np.random.standard_normal((100,10)), reduce='NotAModel', ndims=2)
findings.expected: ValueError naming the unknown model and listing supported names (like hyp.align's), without embedded whitespace artifacts or a stale URL.
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce          for supported models

findings.title: animate.py's 'plays in real time / total ~= duration seconds' claim is 10% off at the default frame_rate=30: PillowWriter emits 30 ms frames, so a 2 s animation plays in 1.80 s
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from PIL import Image
d = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(7).standard_normal((300,10)), axis=0)
hyp.plot(d, animate='window', duration=2, frame_rate=30, save_path='w.gif', show=False)
im = Image.open('w.gif'); im.seek(0)
print(im.n_frames, im.info['duration'])  # 60, 30 -> 1.80 s total
findings.expected: 60 frames x 33.33 ms ~= 2.0 s playback, per the comment.

findings.title: Default animation export (duration=30 x frame_rate=30 = 900 frames) costs 46 s and a 19.7 MB gif for a tiny 300x10 dataset, with no documentation of the cost
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp, time
d = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(7).standard_normal((300,10)), axis=0)
t0=time.time(); hyp.plot(d, animate=True, save_path='default.gif', show=False); print(time.time()-t0)
findings.expected: Default-parameter animation export is either fast/small or its cost is documented where save_path/duration are described.
findings.actual: animate=True DEFAULT (900 frames) gif save: 46.10s wall, size=19.70MB

findings.title: plot() ndims docstring still says 'If ndims > 3, will plot in 3 dimensions but return the higher dimensional data' -- stale in 1.0, where plot() returns a matplotlib Figure
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp

findings.title: Misspelled/unknown **kwargs to plot() only fail deep inside matplotlib (AttributeError from Line2D.set) after the full reduce/align pipeline has already run
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot(np.random.standard_normal((100,10)), bananas=7, show=False)
findings.expected: Fast, hypertools-level error (or warning) naming the unknown kwarg before the pipeline runs, mirroring the plotly backend's upfront unmapped-kwargs warning.
findings.actual: AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'bananas' (raised after format/reduce ran)
